title: Wat kost het? — geld en grote getallen
summary: Hundreds and thousands, euro amounts, and reading prices like €3,50 aloud

blocks.title: Hundreds and thousands
blocks.body: *honderd* (100) and *duizend* (1000) work like the tens: stack a unit in front and keep it one word. And you **don't** say 'een honderd' — plain *honderd* already means one hundred.

blocks.title: Tap to hear the big ones
How the Dutch say a price
blocks.body: The comma is the decimal point: **€3,50** is written with a comma and said *drie euro vijftig*. The trick: say the euros, the word *euro*, then the cents as a plain number — **no** 'cent' needed. Note *euro* never adds an -s here: *twee euro*, not 'twee euro's'.

pairs.note: The cents are just the reversed-tens number you drilled yesterday.
Under a euro, drop 'euro' and say the cents with *cent*.

blocks.explain: Euros, then *euro*, then the cents as one number: *vier euro vijfenzeventig*. You never say 'komma' out loud for money.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the price in Dutch words.
